- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if true outcome shows mean reversion or rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust based on sentiment decay.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model fails to anticipate sharp drop; add a 2–3% downward correction if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model tends to lag; apply early correction with 1–2% buffer below historical mean.
- Sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.33) suggests model overfits trend; use smoothing or reduce slope of forecast curve.
